**Answer each of the following questions with *one sentence* including a brief explanation.**

1.  Finish the sentence with another student’s name: "If \[Name of Student\] doesn’t earn an A, then nobody should, because..." Explain your choice and your reasoning.

    Isaiah (I don't know his last name, he's the biology master's student), because I was impressed that although he had never done programming, he was a great programmer in that he didn't just rush into typing things and was quickly understanding the functions we used, for what purpose, and how they worked.

2.  What was the most difficult part of the class for you? List a general topic, a specific problem, a kind of work we did, etc. and explain why.

    Generally, pivoting is difficult, because I feel like the arguments aren't so obvious as to what they do.

3.  What was the easiest part of the class for you? Explain why.

    I think relational data since I've taken so many classes on relational data and it has been reviewed (so many times).

4.  What part of the class surprised or interested you the most? Explain why.

    I think the most interesting part will be functions, since I like my algorithm design class now.

5.  Give one piece of advice to a student just beginning a quarter of STAT 331 that will help them be successful in learning.

    I think starting the lab as early as possible so as to give yourself room to really read through documentation and stumble across other information in pursuit of the function you're looking for is the best way to go.
